Vulva cancer is predominantly a disease of older women. Squamous cell carcinoma is the most common histological type, usually arising from premalignant lesions, such as vulva intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN). Risk factors contributing to the development of VIN and later vulva cancer include HPV infection, immunosuppression, including infection with HIV, history of genital warts, multiple sexual partners, and cigarette smoking.

There are three (3) types of ovarian cancer. These are epithelial ovarian cancers, which develop from the ovarian epithelial layer; germ cell tumors, which arise from the ovarian cortex; and sex cord stromal tumors, which arise from stromal cells within the cortex. Management of the three histological types of ovarian cancer differs. Epithelial tumors comprise 90% of all ovarian malignancies. Due to anatomical location, most patients present with advanced disease.
